not_evidence: HAND-WRITTEN. Every element prop, value token and rule property here was read off the two files that decide behaviour — form-editor/builder/element-catalog.config.ts (which gates the builder UI) and records/form/view-element.component.svelte (which gates runtime) — not off the Form Creator spec, which disagrees with the renderer in three places. It is not proof the platform renders it: tools/push-form-elements.mjs pushes it to staging so it can be checked in the UI.
teaches: element nodes RENDER now: record-view-renderer gained an `{:else if view.type === 'element'}` branch handing the node to view-element.component.svelte. Before that they fell through to the FIELD renderer and their children were silently dropped
there are exactly seven kinds: text-heading, text-paragraph, text-note, text-link, alert (leaves) and card, card-collapsable (containers)
a CONTAINER element's children are grid ROWS, laid out exactly like the top level — a field placed straight into a card skips the row layer
leaf elements take no children; anything nested in one is dropped
element rules ARE evaluated (view-element receives the whole node and reads node.rules itself) — unlike the array-field repeater, whose own rules are still never passed to ViewRepeater
text-note aligns with `align`; text-heading and text-paragraph use `textAlign`. The builder writes textAlign on a note, which the renderer ignores — see divergences_verified
text-note and text-paragraph carry content in `markdown`, but a `text` RULE is what overrides it (element-catalog ruleTargets)
alert.showSeverityIcon defaults to TRUE — the renderer tests `props.showSeverityIcon !== false`, so only an explicit false hides the icon
card accent "none" is normalised to undefined by the renderer, so it is the same as omitting it

divergences_verified.why: The builder catalog, the Form Creator spec and the runtime renderer disagree in three places. RUNTIME WINS, because that is what a stored config actually does. Each was read off both files.

text-note alignment.runtime: view-element.component.svelte renders a note with align={str('align') ?? 'default'} — it reads props.align.
text-note alignment.builder: element-catalog.config.ts gives text-note a prop editor keyed textAlign.
text-note alignment.verdict: FRONTEND BUG. Aligning a note in the visual builder writes a key the renderer never reads, so it does nothing. This example authors `align`. text-heading and text-paragraph genuinely use `textAlign`, so the inconsistency is real.

card visible rules.runtime: both the card and card-collapsable branches are wrapped in {#if !ruleState.visible}, so a visible rule hides the card and everything in it.
card visible rules.builder: allowedRuleProperties for card and card-collapsable omit 'visible'.
card visible rules.verdict: Safe to author (this example does, on the Cover card) but the builder's Rules tab will not offer it and may not round-trip it.

repeater visible rules.runtime: record-view-renderer passes schema/fieldRef/childNodes/value/errors/nodeProps/onChange to ViewRepeater and NEVER passes rules, so an array-field's own rules are not evaluated.
repeater visible rules.spec: the Form Creator spec claims the repeater container supports `visible`.
repeater visible rules.verdict: The spec is wrong. A visible rule on an array-field is inert — put it on the enclosing grid row. This example therefore uses no repeater rule.

corpus_context.the_one_element: sc8DhU6CEXh4gkJPnS_Le carries the only element node on staging — an element: "card" with correctly-rowed children. It did NOT render before this release and does now, so that config's form gained a card it was previously missing.
corpus_context.no_legacy_shape: Zero configs use type "element" without an `element` kind. That shape would render NOTHING now (view-element derives kind from node.element and its branch chain has no final else), so the validator warns about it even though nothing live is affected.

how_to_verify_on_staging: validate_record_config with this config — expect valid with no warnings
create_record_config, then open the form's Preview tab (the Edit tab sets pointer-events: none, so inputs will not respond there)

check each element: the large heading with its info icon, the intro paragraph, the warning alert, the primary-accented Cover card, the quiet note inside it, the collapsed Portal card, and the terms link
leave `terms_accepted` unticked: the alert must be visible. Tick it: the alert must disappear (element visible rules)
type a legal name: the alert's severity must switch from info to warning, and the Cover card must appear (card visible rule — the one the builder will not let you author)
leave `sum_insured` empty: the Excess slider must be disabled
expand Portal & integrations and toggle Enable portal access: the API key field appears
clean up with delete_record_config (which also purges its records)
